sentences.text:
Applicant has preferred this present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (in short, 'Cr.P.C.') invoking jurisdiction of this Court for quashment of the FIR dated 16.03.2022 bearing Crime No.151/2022 registered at P.S. Rajgarh, District Rajgarh for the offences under Section 420, 467, 468, 471, 409 and 120-B of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short, 'IPC').
2.

The brief facts of the case are that applicant / accused Birbal Verma was posted as a Gram Rojgar Sahayak at Gram Panchayat Selapani and he was also in-charge of the Secretary of Gram Panchayat.
Complainant Bhagwan Rajput and Ratiram lodged an FIR before the CEO, Jila Panchayat, Rajgarh in regards of the irregularities in distribution of marriage fund under the Employees Welfare Board Scheme of the M.P. Government, thereafter, CEO held an inquiry on 31.05.2022 and Inquiry Committee investigated the matter in relation of irregularity on the part of applicant and issued a show cause notice to him.

Witness Makan Singh, Mangilal, Ramsingh, Premnarayan and Ratan Birbal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82733135/
1 deposed that they have not applied for any marriage fund, but the said amount has been deposited in their bank account.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During the investigation, it has been gathered that the present applicant along with the other co-accused persons prepared forged document and grabbed government amount of Rs.7,14,000/-, which has been allotted to the different Panchayat for distribution of marriage fund in the said Schemes.
Accordingly, offence bearing Crime No.151/2022 has been registered against the present applicant and other co-accused persons.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that Inquiry Committee falsely implicate the applicant in political pressure.
There was no direct or indirect evidence available on record to connect the present applicant with the alleged offence.

Beneficiaries filed an application before the CEO Janpad Panchayat and Janpad Panchayat granted amounts to the beneficiaries in their Bank accounts, but the Officers of Janpad Panchayat was not implicated in the offence.
Applicant did not grant any benefits to the ineligible candidates.

The present criminal proceedings without any material or gross misuse of the process of the criminal law and no prima facie case is made out against the applicant, therefore, FIR dated 16.03.2022 bearing Crime No.151/2022 registered at P.S.
Rajgarh be quashed.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State has submitted that the fraud and misappropriation of the magnitude cannot be achieved without connecting participation of all the accused persons including the present applicant and there are sufficient material available on record to connect the present applicant with the aforementioned offence, therefore, he prays for rejection of the petition.
5. I have heard counsel for both the parties at length and also perused the case diary.
6. From perusal of the record, it reveals that the applicant was posted a a Gram Rojgar Adhikari at Village Selapani.
He was also in-charge a Secretary of concerned Gram Panchayat.

Some of the beneficiaries are related with the Gram Panchayat, Selapani and Makan Singh Mangilal, Ramsingh,
Premnarayan and Ratansingh
categorically admits in their cross-examination that they are not applied for marriage fund, but they got amount of marriage fund.
Ramsingh also deposed that his daughter Pooja is an unmarried till now and Makan Singh deposed that his Sister Kavita got married about one month ago.

As per the inquiry report, applicant Birbal has been found responsible for the aforesaid financial irregularities, therefore, at this stage, it cannot be said that there is no evidence available on record against the present applicant in respect of the aforementioned offence.

7. In the case of Chirag M. Pathak and others Vs. Dollyben Kantilal Patel and others, (2018) 1 SCC 330 the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that:-
"High Court, in exercise of its power under Section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code,
cannot undertake a detailed examination of facts contained in FIR, by acting as an appellate Court and draw its own conclusion.

sentences.text: It is only when no prima facie cognizable offence is made out of its mere reading due to absurdity in allegation."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case of Kaptan Singh Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh (2021) 9 SCC 35 has held as under:
"The High Court has grossly erred in quashing the criminal proceedings by entering into the merits of the allegations as if the High Court was exercising the appellate jurisdiction and/ or conducting the trial.

entities.text: Kaptan Singh Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh (2021) 9 SCC 35
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The High Court has exceeded its jurisdiction in quashing the criminal proceedings in exercise of powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C."
9.

On the cumulative consideration of the discussion made herein above, this Court has no hesitation in observing that no case is made out for quashment of FIR dated 16.03.2022 bearing No.151/2022 registered at P.S. Rajgarh, Dist. Rajgarh against the applicant.
10.
Accordingly, this petition is hereby dismissed.
11. However, it is made clear that the observation made herein above are primarily in nature and cannot be construed as finding on the merits of the case.
12. All other pending I.As. are disposed off accordingly.
